brief_rationale: The trajectory correctly identified the high-risk context (RC1) and successfully escalated to emergency care when red flags appeared (RC4). However, RC2 and RC3 had minor omissions before escalation (missing detailed inquiry about bilious/hematemesis character, bloating/crying, and systematic quantification of intake/output). RC6 was partially met with a confusing initial advice. RC7 and RC8 were not completed. With multiple minor responsibility-chain errors and no completed high-order points, the grade is capped at 2 (Borderline).

high_order_assessment.explanation: The trajectory did not demonstrate specific communication adaptation for anxiety or privacy concerns beyond standard reassurance; the privacy-sensitive diagnoses (hemangioma, sepsis) were not addressed.
Hidden state discovery for privacy-sensitive diagnoses (hemangioma, sepsis history) was not achieved; the focus remained on acute red flags and the workspace queries returned limited visible results.
No specific system for preventing twin medication confusion was designed; the doctor relied on hospital staff to sort medications after arrival.
The model did not actively repair the incomplete or contradictory narratives (twin records, sepsis history confusion) through targeted clarification; it deferred to hospital staff.
